problem.text: The existing distribution diagnostic always computed a normalized codebook reference. This change adds standalone integer histogram counts and makes that reference optional.

reasoning.text: A single CUDA block accumulates counts in shared memory, avoiding a separate inter-block reduction. This favors implementation simplicity over scalable parallelism.

impact.text: The extension exposes histogram(input, output, min_value, max_value, exclusive). No Python workflow integration is added; the parent-tree test_distribution search finds only native declarations, its binding and a commented Python call.

source_notes.text: The earlier 00bbb583 entry establishes the original diagnostic's two normalized histograms and records an unchecked destination-capacity concern.

Issues #6 (“No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr'”), #7 (“quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate”) and #29 (“Auto-YaRN for Qwen3? Maybe even set it dynamically?”) concern installation or RoPE behavior. Their relationship here is only an inferred shared-file association through rope.py, whose task edit removes GPTJ from a TODO comment, not executable code.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” discusses codebook experimentation; issues #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” and #42, “converting to 3.0 bpw causes error; block state has 0 inf values and 34 NaN values,” report conversion failures. Their association is inferred from the inspected quantize.py path and codebook context, not an explicit link to this histogram change.

limitations: No extension build or CUDA execution was performed; launch success, synchronization behavior and performance remain unmeasured.
The scalar transcription uses small, exactly representable finite values. It does not establish CUDA float-to-integer behavior for nonfinite or extreme values, counter overflow, or invalid ranges.
Literal caller searches do not exclude external or dynamically constructed extension calls.

chapters.title: Standalone counts and optional reference distributions

claims.text: histogram accepts float32 or float16 input and requires a kLong output, despite the comment describing uint64_t. It uses the input device/current CUDA stream, derives the bin count from output.numel(), and launches one block of 1024 threads. Each thread traverses every 1024th input element; shared unsigned 64-bit counters are cleared, atomically incremented and copied over the output.

For ordinary finite values and a positive range, indexing truncates (value-min)/(max-min)*num_bins and clamps to the endpoint bins. exclusive=true discards values strictly outside the range but retains both endpoints; false folds outliers into endpoint counts. Unlike test_distribution, these outputs are counts, not normalized probability masses.

A scalar transcription with four bins over [-1,1] and samples [-2,-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1,2] produced [2,1,1,3] without exclusion and [1,1,1,2] with exclusion. Arithmetic also confirms 8192 bytes for 1024 eight-byte counters and 64 reference states per thread when enumerating all 65,536 uint16 states.

test_distribution now accepts an optional reference tensor. OPTPTR maps an absent value to nullptr, and a uniform pointer guard skips reference clearing, decoding and writing. Bin count now comes from dist_output, with equal element counts checked when the reference pointer is non-null. These coordinated changes let input-only diagnostics run without a reference allocation.

The header and implementation agree on the changed signature, while the binding still exposes the same function name. The only Python call found remains commented and supplies the older five-argument form, omitting the two multiplier arguments already required in the parent; it is not an active compatible caller.

The specific undersized-dist_output scenario recorded by the ancestor entry is removed for non-null reference buffers: the task derives the write length from dist_output and rejects unequal reference lengths before launch. This does not establish comprehensive tensor validation.

findings.description: The new histogram wrapper permits zero bins although counting requires a valid bin.
findings.trigger: Call histogram with nonempty contiguous CUDA float input, an empty kLong output, min_value=0, max_value=1 and exclusive=false.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject the zero-bin output before launching.
findings.actual_behavior: The sole bin-count guard accepts zero. For an input value of zero, idx becomes zero, the unsigned comparison succeeds, and num_bins-1 underflows before assignment to idx; the subsequent atomic update has no valid initialized histogram bin. Reach is direct extension callers; no parent-tree callers of the new utility were found.

verification.description: Traced output.numel() through the upper-bound-only check, shared-memory initialization and index clamp.
verification.limits: No malformed CUDA invocation was executed; the resulting device error or memory effect is unmeasured.

annotation.summary: Adds a float16/float32 CUDA counting histogram and optional codebook references, fixes the prior reference/output length mismatch, and leaves a suspected zero-bin validation gap.

for exclusive in (False,True):
 h=[0]*4
 for x in xs:
  if exclusive and (x < -1 or x > 1): continue
  idx=int((x+1)/2*4);idx=max(0,min(3,idx));h[idx]+=1
 print(exclusive,h,sum(h))
